symptom: scripts/build-locked.ps1 failed in about 1.6 s, before dotnet ran, when given extra dotnet arguments: '/v:q' right after -Project failed the Configuration ValidateSet; '-v:q' failed with 'Cannot convert System.String to SwitchParameter' on -Verbose; '-p:Name=Value' failed with 'parameter p is specified more than once'; '-bl:path' reached MSBuild as '-bl:' and 'path', which read the path as a second project (MSB1008).
cause: [CmdletBinding()] made every unattributed parameter positional, so the first unnamed token after -Project bound to -Configuration (position 1). Separately, PowerShell reads any '-name:value' token as one of its own parameters, prefix-matched against the script's and the common ones, before ValueFromRemainingArguments sees it. Reproduced on 2026-11-07 on a copy of the param block, called with -File and directly; '--' does not help in either mode.
violatedInvariant: Extra arguments given to build-locked.ps1 reach dotnet unchanged; the script's own parameters bind only by name (comment at the CmdletBinding line, usage in the header).

must: Keep [CmdletBinding(PositionalBinding = $false)] so an extra argument never lands in -Configuration.
Write extra MSBuild switches in the slash form (/v:q, /bl:path, /p:Name=Value) and dotnet options with two dashes (--no-restore).
mustNot: Pass dotnet arguments of the form -name:value: PowerShell captures or splits them whatever the param block.

automation.residual: The test checks positional binding through PowerShell's static binder without running dotnet. The -name:value traps are PowerShell's parsing rules and are documented, not tested.
